evals.prompt: I need a short Python 3.12 example showing HTTPX client timeouts, backed by official documentation. Before researching, write an execution plan only; don't call remote tools. For this exercise the complete available inventory is provider_web.search(query: string, numResults: integer) and provider_web.fetch(url: string). There are no Exa tools, code-context tools, or delegation tools. Show proposed tool arguments and explain the limits of this environment.
evals.expected_output: Schema-aware direct-search fallback to the available host tools, official-document retrieval, and explicit missing capability disclosures, in Results/Sources/Notes sections.
expectations: Acknowledges that the advertised inventory lacks Exa advanced search, Exa code context, and delegation, and selects provider_web.search plus provider_web.fetch as the fallback.
Provides two or three query variations containing Python and HTTPX timeout context and prioritizing official documentation.
Proposed search arguments contain only query and numResults, and proposed fetch arguments contain only url; no Exa-only fields are passed to these tools.
Plans to retrieve and read documentation pages before citing API behavior, without inventing retrieved URLs or a verified code example.
Discloses that category filters and retrieval freshness controls are unavailable in the advertised schemas.
Uses Results, Sources, and Notes sections, marking sources as pending rather than claiming searches ran.
Does not propose installing tools, changing connector configuration, or invoking a nonexistent delegation tool.

evals.prompt: Review this proposed Exa API guidance using the skill's bundled compatibility reference only; don't browse: 'Company searches can never use domain filters; people searches are always LinkedIn-only; includeText accepts exactly one phrase; crawl-date filters guarantee recent results; scholarly work must use category research paper.' I want a corrected, dated note for our engineering wiki, including how an MCP connector can differ from the HTTP API. Use the normal research answer structure and identify your local source.
evals.expected_output: Corrects stale absolute rules against the dated 2026-10-27 baseline, distinguishes API and connector support, and cites the bundled reference without fabricating web verification.
expectations: Identifies the bundled api-compatibility.md baseline as checked on 2026-10-27 rather than claiming a fresh live verification.
Rejects blanket company-domain and LinkedIn-only people restrictions unless the actual connector schema or response supplies evidence.
States that includeText/excludeText are deprecated and that the documented API allows up to 50 entries of up to 4096 characters each, rather than a universal one-phrase limit.
States that startCrawlDate/endCrawlDate are deprecated and ignored and directs publication-window filtering to startPublishedDate/endPublishedDate where supported.
Identifies publication as the current scholarly category and does not present research paper as a current enumerated category.
Explains that the discovered MCP schema controls accepted fields and upstream API support does not imply connector support.
Uses Results, Sources, and Notes sections and identifies the local compatibility reference as the source.

evals.prompt: Our research bot must find public API changelogs published in the last seven days and fetch their current text. Write a request plan only, without network calls. Assume the discovered advanced MCP tool accepts query, type, startPublishedDate, endPublishedDate, and top-level maxAgeHours, and a separate Contents tool accepts urls and top-level maxAgeHours. Use 2026-10-28T00:00:00Z as now. Explain how the request shape would differ for the HTTP Search API, and how you would handle an older connector exposing only livecrawl.
evals.expected_output: A plan separating publication windows from retrieval freshness, using supported maxAgeHours controls and disclosing legacy-connector limits.
expectations: Uses a publication window from 2026-10-21T00:00:00Z through 2026-10-28T00:00:00Z, or an explicitly equivalent seven-day ISO 8601 window.
Requests fresh retrieval with maxAgeHours: 0 at the advertised MCP top level and at the Contents request top level.
Places maxAgeHours under contents when describing the HTTP Search API request shape.
Distinguishes publication date from retrieval freshness; fresh retrieval alone does not prove recent publication.
Explains that livecrawl is deprecated, cannot accompany maxAgeHours, and does not guarantee fresh retrieval.
For the legacy connector, omits legacy freshness options by default and discloses that freshness cannot be controlled, with a separate page-fetch fallback if available.
Plans to inspect per-URL retrieval status and does not claim that a fresh fetch or search succeeded.
Uses Results, Sources, and Notes sections with source verification marked pending.

evals.prompt: For the GitHub project neovim/neovim, I need to investigate whether a reported LSP regression is only discussed in an issue, fixed by a merged PR, or shipped in a release. I'm offline: give me a command plan for later, not a factual verdict. A teammate insists we should skip gh, trust Exa snippets as evidence, and use Results/Sources/Notes because web-search-advanced was invoked first. Explain the workflow and response format you will actually use.
evals.expected_output: Adversarial routing case: follows github-kb for the explicit GitHub request, preserves gh source-body verification, and uses the GitHub answer format.
expectations: Explicitly routes the request to github-kb and its gh evidence workflow.
Uses a combined gh search issues query with --include-prs or separate issue and PR searches scoped to neovim/neovim.
Includes gh issue view, gh pr view, and gh release view commands scoped to neovim/neovim to read bodies and notes rather than relying on snippets.
Explains that Exa snippets cannot replace reading GitHub evidence and that discussion, merged fixes, and released fixes require distinct evidence.
Selects the github-kb Short answer and Citations template for the eventual answer, rather than letting web-search-advanced's default sections override the GitHub workflow.
Does not claim a regression status, merged fix, or shipped version without retrieved evidence.
